daily.ideas: Economic Viewpoint: MY Industrial Production (Aug-26); Weekly Technical Review: DJIA, KLCI

news.h: PMB Technology plans RM650.0m silicon-aluminium alloy plant in Sarawak
news.body: PMB Technology Bhd, a 58.8%-owned subsidiary of Press Metal Aluminium Holdings Bhd, plans to invest RM650.0m to build a silicon-aluminium (Si-Al) alloy plant in Sarawak as the group seeks to diversify away from a struggling silicon metal business. The aluminium product maker said the proposed plant would be located at Samalaju Industrial Park, where the group's existing silicon metal manufacturing operations are based. Construction is expected to be completed, with commercial operations commencing, by the second quarter of 2027, PMB Technology said in a bourse filing. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: PMB Technology plans to invest RM650.0m in a silicon-aluminium alloy plant.
The plant will be at Samalaju Industrial Park, Sarawak, next to the group's existing silicon metal operations.
The stated aim is to diversify away from a struggling silicon metal business.
Construction and the start of commercial operations are targeted for 2Q27. The item does not say how the plant is funded or what capacity it will have.

PMB Technology is 58.8% owned by Press Metal. This board's only PMETAL row is Kenanga's 28 August Results Note (MARKET PERFORM, target RM8.80), which has no bearing on this item. The board holds no Kenanga coverage of PMB Technology. Digest context only.

news.h: Hektar REIT aborts RM26.0m deal for Perlis land for solar farm project
news.body: Hektar Real Estate Investment Trust (Hektar REIT) has terminated its proposed RM26.0m acquisition of a 90.0% stake in Terramark Sdn Bhd, citing the sellers' failure to fulfil several key conditions precedent. The retail-focused REIT said it had aborted plans to acquire 16.3m shares in Terramark from Wan Realty Sdn Bhd and Darul Modal Sdn Bhd. It did not specify which conditions had not been met. The deposit paid for the proposed acquisition will be refunded, Hektar REIT said, adding that the termination is not expected to have a material impact on its earnings, net asset value, gearing, unitholders' capital or substantial unitholders' holdings for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Hektar REIT has ended its proposed RM26.0m purchase of 90.0% of Terramark Sdn Bhd, or 16.3m shares.
It says the sellers, Wan Realty Sdn Bhd and Darul Modal Sdn Bhd, failed to meet several key conditions precedent. It does not say which ones.
The price valued all of Terramark at about RM28.9m (computed here). The Perlis land and solar farm come from the headline; the body does not describe them.
The deposit will be refunded. Hektar expects no material impact on earnings, NAV or gearing for FY ending 31 December 2026.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Hektar REIT. Digest context only.

news.h: EP Manufacturing, China's Hebei Shichang to invest RM100.0m in Selangor fuel tank plant
news.body: EP Manufacturing Bhd has formed a joint venture (JV) with Beijing-listed Hebei Shichang Auto Parts Co Ltd to invest RM100.0m in a new fuel tank manufacturing facility in Selangor to supply Proton Holdings Bhd, as the automaker expands production and deepens local sourcing. The automotive solutions provider said its wholly-owned subsidiary Fundwin Sdn Bhd had signed a JV agreement with Hebei Shichang to establish EP Shichang Automotive Systems Sdn Bhd. EP Manufacturing will hold a 51.0% stake in the venture, with Hebei Shichang owning the remaining 49.0%. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: EP Manufacturing and Hebei Shichang Auto Parts plan to invest RM100.0m in a fuel tank plant in Selangor.
The plant will supply Proton, which the item says is expanding production and sourcing more locally.
The JV company is EP Shichang Automotive Systems Sdn Bhd. EP Manufacturing holds 51.0% through wholly owned Fundwin Sdn Bhd, and Hebei Shichang holds 49.0%.
The item does not say how the RM100.0m is split between the partners or when the plant will start.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of EP Manufacturing. Digest context only.

news.h: Astral Asia explores RM234.0m Kuantan land sale to HNG Capital
news.body: Astral Asia Bhd is exploring the sale of 2,433 acres of land at the Kuantan Hi-Tech Park in Pahang to HNG Capital Sdn Bhd for RM233.6m. HNG Capital was formerly known as Leader Universal Holdings Bhd before the group was taken private by the H'ng family in 2011. The proposed disposal could pave the way for solar farm and green energy development. The diversified group said that its subsidiary Astral Asia Plantation Sdn Bhd (AAP) had entered into a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with HNG Capital for the proposed disposal. The land accounts for 25.0% of Astral Asia's total land area. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Astral Asia is exploring the sale of 2,433 acres at Kuantan Hi-Tech Park, Pahang, to HNG Capital Sdn Bhd. The body gives the price as RM233.6m; the headline rounds it to RM234.0m.
That is about RM96,000 an acre, or about RM2.20 per sq ft (computed here).
This is a memorandum of understanding signed by subsidiary Astral Asia Plantation Sdn Bhd, not a binding sale agreement.

The land is 25.0% of Astral Asia's total land area. The item says the sale could open the way to solar and green energy development. HNG Capital is the former Leader Universal Holdings, taken private by the H'ng family in 2011.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Astral Asia. Digest context only.

news.h: AIMAX to sell two firms to Datasonic for RM15.1m to partially settle debt
news.body: AIMAX Bhd, formerly known as Hong Seng Consolidated Bhd, has agreed to sell two companies to Datasonic Group Bhd for a combined RM15.1m as part of a plan to partially settle an outstanding debt owed by the group. Under a share sale agreement (SSA), AIMAX will dispose of its entire equity interest in IF Security Solution Sdn Bhd (IFSS), comprising one million shares, to Datasonic for RM1.0m. Separately, AIMAX's wholly-owned subsidiary AIMAX Assets Sdn Bhd has agreed to sell its entire equity interest in Premiumway Development Sdn Bhd (PDSB), also comprising one million shares, to Datasonic for RM14.1m. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: AIMAX, formerly Hong Seng Consolidated, is selling two companies to Datasonic Group for a combined RM15.1m.
IF Security Solution Sdn Bhd goes for RM1.0m. Premiumway Development Sdn Bhd, held through wholly owned AIMAX Assets Sdn Bhd, goes for RM14.1m. The two add up to the RM15.1m total (computed here).
The sale is part of a plan to partly settle an outstanding debt owed by the AIMAX group.
The item does not say who the debt is owed to, how large it is, or what the two companies earn.
This board holds no Kenanga coverage of AIMAX or Datasonic. Digest context only.

macro.h: China says can avoid 'escalation' after EU trade talks
macro.body: China and the European Union can avoid "escalation" in various contentious disputes, Beijing said on Saturday, as worries of a damaging trade war simmer. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Beijing says China and the EU can avoid escalation in several disputes.
The statement came on Saturday, after trade talks.
The item points to ongoing worries about a damaging trade war.
The item does not name the disputes or give any figures.
Digest context only; sourced to The Edge Malaysia.

macro.h: A wider safety net on the same thin revenue base (Economic Viewpoint: Malaysia 2027 Federal Budget)
macro.body: Most inclusive MADANI budget yet, but light on revenue. Budget 2027 extends relief to the M40 and MSMEs with no new broad-based tax, which leaves consolidation more reliant on oil. We see the 2027 deficit at 3.4% of GDP against the MoF's 3.3%, and it could reach 3.5% if election-year spending rises. (Economic Viewpoint: Malaysia 2027 Federal Budget)
takeaways: This is Kenanga's own summary of Budget 2027. It calls it the most inclusive MADANI budget yet, but light on revenue.
Relief is extended to the M40 and MSMEs, with no new broad-based tax. Kenanga says that leaves fiscal consolidation more reliant on oil.
Kenanga sees the 2027 deficit at 3.4% of GDP, against the Finance Ministry's 3.3%. It could reach 3.5% if election-year spending rises.
The full note is not in today's bundle. Kenanga's site lists it in its 10 October edition, which this board does not carry, so nothing here goes beyond the digest summary.
Digest context only; sourced to Kenanga's Economic Viewpoint as summarised in today's digest.

macro.h: Jobless rate dips to 2.9% on robust hiring, but October layoff surge is the number to watch (See Economic Viewpoint: Malaysia Labour Market)
macro.body: The unemployment rate fell to 2.9% in August (Jul: 3.0%), reflecting better job market conditions. We keep our 2026 unemployment rate forecast at 2.9% (2025: 3.0%) on strong growth prospect. (See Economic Viewpoint: Malaysia Labour Market)
takeaways: Unemployment fell to 2.9% in August from 3.0% in July.
Kenanga keeps its 2026 unemployment forecast at 2.9% (2025: 3.0%), citing strong growth prospects.
The headline names an October layoff surge as the figure to watch. The summary gives no number for it.
July's 3.0% matches Kenanga's 14 September Labour Market note on this board. The full August note is in Kenanga's 9 October bundle, not today's, and is not carried on this board.
Digest context only; sourced to Kenanga's Economic Viewpoint as summarised in today's digest.

macro.h: Malaysia's IPI expands 4.7% in July, manufacturing sales hit RM177.3b
macro.body: Malaysia's Industrial Production Index (IPI) expanded 4.7 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y) in July 2026, supported by growth in the manufacturing and electricity sectors, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM). (The Star)
takeaways: The item reports July 2026 IPI growth of 4.7% YoY, supported by manufacturing and electricity.
That is the previous month's print. Kenanga's IPI note in today's bundle agrees July was 4.7% and gives August at 5.0%.
The RM177.3b manufacturing sales figure is in the headline only. The body does not say which month it covers.
In Kenanga's note, mining fell 3.2% in July, consistent with the item naming only manufacturing and electricity as sources of growth.
Digest context only; sourced to The Star.

macro.h: Malaysia's wholesale, retail trade sales rise 10.5% to RM173b in August - DOSM
macro.body: Malaysia's wholesale and retail trade recorded sales of RM173 billion in August 2026, an increase of 10.5 per cent year-on-year (y-o-y), said the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DoSM). (The Star)
takeaways: Wholesale and retail trade sales were RM173b in August 2026.
That is 10.5% higher than a year earlier, which implies about RM156.6b in August 2025 (computed here).
The figures come from the Department of Statistics.
The item gives no split between wholesale, retail and motor vehicles, and no month-on-month change.
Digest context only; sourced to The Star.

macro.h: Anwar: Malaysia, Egypt to expand trade, investment and economic cooperation
macro.body: Malaysia and Egypt will focus on expanding trade and investment cooperation, improving flight connectivity and exploring new areas of economic collaboration at a Joint Commission meeting in the first quarter of next year. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Malaysia and Egypt plan to expand trade and investment cooperation.
They will also look at better flight connections and new areas of economic collaboration.
These will be discussed at a Joint Commission meeting in 1Q27.
The item gives no trade or investment figures.
Digest context only; sourced to The Edge Malaysia.

macro.h: China added 10.52m urban jobs in January-September, to roll out services jobs policy
macro.body: China added 10.52 million urban jobs in the first nine months of the year, meeting 87.7% of its annual target, the labour ministry said on Saturday. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: China added 10.52m urban jobs in January-September.
That is 87.7% of the annual target, which implies a target of about 12.0m (computed here).
The headline says a policy on services jobs will follow. The body gives no detail.
The figures come from China's labour ministry, released on Saturday.
Digest context only; sourced to The Edge Malaysia.

macro.h: US consumer sentiment near record low as frustration over economy mounts
macro.body: US consumer sentiment slumped further in early October as the rising cost of living because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy, more bad news for President Donald Trump ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: US consumer sentiment fell further in early October and is near a record low.
The item blames the rising cost of living linked to the Middle East conflict.
It frames this as bad news for President Trump ahead of the 3 November midterms.
The item gives no index reading.
Digest context only; sourced to The Edge Malaysia.

macro.h: Proposed next EU budget slashed by EUR140.0b — official
macro.body: Ireland, which holds the EU's rotating presidency, suggested Saturday on slashing the bloc's next proposed budget by EUR140 billion (USD155 billion), a new draft showed, in a search for a deal. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: A new draft would cut the EU's next proposed budget by EUR140b (USD155b).
The proposal comes from Ireland, which holds the EU's rotating presidency.
The item says the aim is to reach a deal.
It does not give the size of the budget being cut or the period it covers.
Digest context only; sourced to The Edge Malaysia.

reports.flag: Four points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) Today's digest carries a July print beside this August note. Its Macro Bits item from The Star reads 'Malaysia's IPI expands 4.7% in July'. This note's Table 1 agrees that July was 4.7%, but August, the latest month, is 5.0%. The digest item is the previous month's figure, not a conflicting one. (2) The sector weights do not reproduce the headline. Table 1 gives 2015-base weights of 68.3% manufacturing, 25.1% mining and 6.6% electricity. Weighting August's sector growth rates by them gives about 3.8%, not 5.0% (computed here). Base-year weights are not current shares of output, so this is not evidence of an error, but the note does not reconcile the two. (3) Graphs 1-3 are charts. Only their titles and sources could be read, and no figure on this row is taken from them. (4) The 10-year averages are the note's own. They are not in Table 1 and cannot be checked against it. This is an Economic Viewpoint and carries no stock call, so the rating, target-price and share-price columns are empty by design and no Analyst Signal is sought.
reports.name: Malaysia Industrial Production (Aug-26): E&E lifts output to 5.0%, supporting 3Q26 GDP growth
reports.catalyst: Industrial production grew 5.0% YoY in August (Jul: 4.7%), beating Kenanga's 4.0% estimate and slightly ahead of the 4.9% consensus. Manufacturing rose to a four-month high of 7.4%, led by E&E at 17.0%, a four-year high. Mining fell 7.4%, its weakest in 15 months. Kenanga raises its 2026 manufacturing IPI forecast to 6.1% from 5.0%, but stays cautious on 4Q26 as domestic-oriented output softens and the favourable base effect fades. It keeps its 2026 GDP forecast at 5.3% and expects 3Q26 GDP growth of 5.1%.
reports.quote: We raise our 2026 manufacturing IPI growth forecast to 6.1% (2025: 4.5%) from 5.0% on sustained E&E strength, but stay cautious on 4Q26
summary: A beat on the headline. IPI grew 5.0% YoY in August from 4.7% in July, against Kenanga's 4.0% estimate and a 4.9% consensus. That is 1.0 percentage point above the house estimate (computed here). Month on month, output rebounded 2.6% after a 2.0% fall in July, above the 10-year average of 1.1%. On Table 1, the seasonally adjusted rate was 4.9% and the three-month moving average eased to 5.4% from 6.5%.

Manufacturing did the work, and E&E drove it. Manufacturing grew 7.4% (Jul: 6.4%), a four-month high, and 3.4% month on month (Jul: -2.0%), above its 10-year average of 1.8%. E&E grew 17.0% (Jul: 13.3%), a four-year high. Export-oriented output rose 9.1% (Jul: 6.7%), also a four-year high. That was led by computer, electronics and optical products at 18.8% (Jul: 14.0%), with coke and refined petroleum at 5.4% (Jul: 1.1%).

The domestic side slowed. Domestic-oriented manufacturing grew 3.9% (Jul: 5.8%), a three-month low, as motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers fell 5.3% after growing 4.2% in July. Kenanga names this softer domestic output, together with a fading favourable base effect, as the reason for caution on 4Q26.

Mining dragged; electricity rose. Mining fell 7.4% (Jul: -3.2%), its weakest in 15 months, on crude petroleum (-12.2%; Jul: -13.1%) and natural gas (-4.3%; Jul: +3.6%). It contracted month on month for a fifth straight month (-0.3%), but by less than July's -4.1% and the 10-year average of -1.7%, which Kenanga reads as an easing pace of decline. Electricity grew 9.0% (Jul: 5.5%), a four-month high, which Kenanga links to commercial activity, household consumption and the weather.

The forecast changes. Manufacturing IPI grew 6.6% in January-August (Jan-Jul: 6.5%). Kenanga raises its 2026 manufacturing IPI forecast to 6.1% from 5.0% (2025: 4.5%) on sustained E&E strength. It says strong July-August manufacturing supports its 5.1% estimate for 3Q26 GDP growth, though persistent mining weakness may cap the upside. It keeps its 2026 GDP forecast at 5.3% (2025: 5.2%) 'for now', the same figure as its 21 September External Trade note on this board.
